To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pion distribution amplitudes are not the same as the pion form factor, and that the pion form factors are not the same in the Drell-Yan reaction as they are in the pion form-factor reaction.
the pion distribution amplitudes are very sensitive to higher twist effects.
the angular distribution of lepton production in Drell‐YaN process is sensitive to higher twist effects and the pion distribution amplitudes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the Drell‐Yang cross section and its angular distribution.
the calculation of the Drell‐yan angular distribution taking into account higher twist effects.
the study of the pion electromagnetic form factor in the timelike region, the pion distribution amplitudes and their evolution with the QCD scale, and their influence on the Drell‐Yang process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are not in agreement with the standard QCD factorization theorem, but are consistent with the predictions of QCD in a bound state framework.
the Drell‐Yang process is not the best process to study the shape of the distribution amplitude of the pion.
the Drell‐Yang process is a very promising tool for testing QCD sum rules predictions for the pion distribution amplitudes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pion distribution amplitudes can be extracted by fitting the data on the angular distribution of leptons in Drell‐Yann process in the kinematical region where one of pion constituents goes off shell.
the Drell‐Yang process is a good probe of the pion structure, which can be used to discriminate between different models for the distribution amplitude.
pion bound state effect is very important in the Drell-Yan process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Drell‐Yang reaction is a powerful tool to study pion structure.
higher twist effects are important for a proper description of the Drell‐yan process.
the Drell‐yan process provides a sensitive probe of the pion wave function.
